:::{#exm-big-omega}
#### The function $3n + 5$ is big-Omega of $n$

Let $f(n) = 3n + 5$ and $g(n) = n$.
To show $f(n) = \Omega(g(n))$ by @def-big-omega,
choose $c = 3$ and $N = 1$.
For every [natural number](number-systems.qmd#def-natural-numbers) $n \ge 1$,

$$
\ba
|f(n)|
&= 3n + 5
&& \text{(} 3n + 5 > 0 \text{)}
\\
&\ge 3n
&& \text{(} 5 \ge 0 \text{)}
\\
&= 3 \, |g(n)|,
&& \text{(} n = |n| \text{, since } n \ge 0 \text{)}
\ea
$$

which is the [inequality](proof-writing.qmd#def-inequality) in @def-big-omega with $c = 3$.
Hence $3n + 5 = \Omega(n)$.

:::
